summary: Most masculine nouns take -ִים (-im) in the plural and most feminine nouns take -וֹת (-ot), replacing a feminine ending -ָה / -ִית / -ִיָּה (עַגְבָנִיָּה → עַגְבָנִיּוֹת, כְּרוּבִית → כְּרוּבִיּוֹת). The stem vowels often shorten (בָּצָל → בְּצָלִים, גֶּזֶר → גְּזָרִים, חָצִיל → חֲצִילִים). Some feminine nouns take -ִים (דְּלַעַת → דְּלוּעִים, כְּרֵשָׁה → כְּרֵשִׁים, אֲפוּנָה → אֲפוּנִים), so the plural has to be learnt with the word. Many food words are mass nouns used in the singular (שׁוּם, בְּרוֹקוֹלִי, תִּירָס). Adjectives agree in number (פִּלְפְּלִים חֲרִיפִים); in a construct phrase only the first noun changes (תַּפּוּחֵי אֲדָמָה).

askYourself: Is the noun masculine or feminine? (Masculine → usually -ִים; feminine → usually -וֹת.)
Does it end in -ָה, -ִית or -ִיָּה? → replace the ending with -וֹת / -ִיּוֹת.
Is it one of the feminine nouns with -ִים (דְּלַעַת, כְּרֵשָׁה, אֲפוּנָה)? → check the word card.
Do the stem vowels shorten (qamats or segol in the first syllable → shva or hataf)?
Is it a mass noun (garlic, broccoli, corn)? → keep the singular.
Is there an adjective or a second noun? → the adjective also becomes plural; in a construct phrase only the first noun changes.

traps: The ending does not always follow the gender: דְּלַעַת (f) → דְּלוּעִים, כְּרֵשָׁה (f) → כְּרֵשִׁים.
The first vowel shortens: בָּצָל → בְּצָלִים, גֶּזֶר → גְּזָרִים, סֶלֶק → סְלָקִים; under a guttural it becomes a hataf: חָצִיל → חֲצִילִים.
-ִיָּה and -ִית become -ִיּוֹת: עַגְבָנִיָּה → עַגְבָנִיּוֹת, כְּרוּבִית → כְּרוּבִיּוֹת.
Food is often a mass noun: קָנִיתִי גֶּזֶר “I bought carrots”; שׁוּם, בְּרוֹקוֹלִי and תִּירָס have no plural in everyday use.
Construct phrase: תַּפּוּחַ אֲדָמָה → תַּפּוּחֵי אֲדָמָה (only the first noun).

seeAlso.note: Arabic has sound plurals like Hebrew -ִים / -וֹת (-ūna / -āt) and also “broken” plurals that change the inside of the word — and a dual.
German has five plural types (-e, -er, -(e)n, -s, umlaut) learned with each noun, as Hebrew plurals are.
Chinese nouns have no plural; 们 is added only to people (朋友们), and numbers use measure words.
